corrections.caveats: ThePhD lua-bindings-shootout (14 stars, run by the sol2 author, no CPU model or compiler version, LuaBridge master unpinned). The 2018-09-28 run timed master between fc224ab (proxy removed, shipped as 2.1) and 74992b8 (proxy restored 2018-10-11), when t[k] = v silently did nothing (issue #171): the table_set and table_chained_set rows failed with 'unexpected result' rather than being unsupported, and the read rows timed code that 2.1.1 replaced. The headline 7.1x set row compares LuaBridge setGlobal (bare push plus lua_setglobal, tying plain C at 15.7 vs 15.1 ns) with luabind's globals() proxy object. Against luabind it wins 8 rows and loses 5 (including c_function_through_lua_in_c 131.1 vs 78.5 and lua_function_in_c 131.8 vs 59.3) and it is slower than the plain Lua C API on every row. The result JSON does not match the committed harness (implicit_inheritance timed but marked unsupported). Not a duplicate of LuaBridge3 (a fork); upstream 2.x still releases (2.10, 2025-10-13).

tier_reason: Lowered B to C: the independent DLPerf numbers come from an asymmetric harness (TensorFlow decodes JPEGs on the GPU through DALI while the PyTorch script is hard-coded to CPU decode; static vs dynamic loss scaling; per-step mean vs time-based throughput), so the margin is not like for like even though NVIDIA's own READMEs keep the ordering.

corrections.claimed_speedup: DLPerf ResNet-50 v1.5 AMP: NGC TensorFlow 1.x with XLA 1198.55 vs NGC PyTorch 802.9 img/s on 1 GPU (1.49x) and 8588.45 vs 6154.66 on 8 GPUs (1.40x); with DLPerf's static-loss-scale PyTorch run the lead is 1.45x/1.33x; NVIDIA READMEs: 1099.55 (1217.90 with XLA) vs 856.52 img/s on 1 V100.
corrections.caveats: GPU JPEG decode (DALI nvJPEG) for TF vs CPU decode for PyTorch; static vs dynamic loss scaling; different throughput definitions; wins only with the NGC build plus XLA and AMP; PyTorch faster in FP32; 2020 numbers; opposite claim to the pytorch/pytorch entry.
